chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazi', from Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him) who said:

Have good thoughts about Allah, for Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'I am according to the thought of My believing servant regarding Me; if [it is] good, then [it is] good, and if [it is] evil, then [it is] evil.'
ai.seo_question: What does it mean that Allah is 'according to the thought of His servant'?
ai.summary: Recorded by Imam al-Rida (AS) in *Al-Kafi*, this hadith elucidates the principle of *al-Husn al-Zann* (good expectation), where God’s response is directly proportional to the servant’s internal perception of Him. This concept serves as a cornerstone of Shia spiritual psychology, encouraging believers to cultivate optimism in divine mercy while remaining mindful that negative expectations can lead to spiritual constriction.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazi’e, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Have good thoughts about Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic is Saying: “I<sup>azwj</sup> Assume the thoughts of My<sup>azwj</sup> believing servant has with Me<sup>azwj</sup> – if good, so good, but if evil, so evil’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Muhammad ibn Isma’il ibn Bazi’ from abu al-Hassan al-Rida (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Be hopeful about Allah, because Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, has said, ‘I deal according to the thinking of My believing servant toward Me. I am good to him if he thinks good about Me and I am not good to him if he does not think good about Me.’”
